note: Order of the guided run (/grammatica/percorso) and of every topic list sorted by level (src/lib/lehrplan.js). This is a teaching decision, not a derived sort: within a level, what later topics build on comes first. Italian order (grammar-structure run, 2026-11-13; slot map in docs/content-plan.md section 3): A1 starts with subject pronouns, then gender, articles, plurals and adjective agreement, numbers, essere/avere and essere/stare, c'è/ci sono, the regular and key irregular presents, questions, e/ma/perché, possessives, demonstratives, piacere and telling the time; A2 starts with frequency adverbs, negation and place (a, in, da, prepositions with articles), then article or none, ordinals and dates, modal verbs and polite requests, the near future and stare + gerund, quantity and the partitive, indefinites, comparatives, adverbs in -mente and perché/siccome, then the passato prossimo (avere, essere), reflexive verbs and the imperfetto, and only then the direct and indirect object pronouns, because they are first used with the passato prossimo; B1 opens with passato prossimo vs imperfetto and the trapassato, then future, conditional, real se-clauses, the imperative, ci/ne and combined pronouns (they build on the A2 pronouns), stressed pronouns, the congiuntivo presente and what follows it, time and purpose clauses, relatives, indirect questions, linkers, fare + infinitive and verbal periphrases, and the refinements; B2 starts with the congiuntivo imperfetto and the periodo ipotetico, because the following subjunctive topics use them; C1 starts with the sequence of tenses and ends with formal style. Only topics listed here are part of the run (core). Topics left out are extra practice (reference and word-formation topics: wortarten, wortbildung-nomen): they keep their page and their place in the index, but they do not lengthen the run. Each topic must be listed under its own `level`. Drafts (status entwurf) only count once they are reviewed. An entry id:A2 would be the A2 part of a topic that teaches two levels on one page (exercise titles starting A2:); no Italian topic does this at the moment. `akkusativ` has its own page (/pronomi-complemento) and is named for the sorted lists, not as a run station. Keep GRAMMATIK_ORDER in src/lib/grammatikOrder.js in step.
